subtype: Stage 4: Forced sorry versus felt sorry [Observer]
passage:
Teacher's note, Sunflower class, pick-up time. Sudha.
Tanvir (5) knocked over Pia's sand castle while waiting for his father. His father saw and said at once, "Say sorry. Now. Say sorry!" Tanvir mumbled "sorry" to the ground and went back to digging. Pia was still crying. The word hadn't reached her. I knelt near them and tried something else. "Tanvir, Pia is sad. What could make her feel a bit better?" He thought, then began scooping sand back into a pile. His father watched, then said to Pia, "I'm sorry too, beta. We rushed him." Tanvir looked up at that. Plan: share this at the next parents' meeting.

qa.q: What did Tanvir knock over?
qa.a: He knocked over Pia's sand castle.

qa.q: What does Tanvir's mumbled "sorry" to the ground suggest?
qa.a: It suggests the word was forced and he didn't yet feel or understand it.

qa.q: What did Sudha's question do that "Say sorry now" didn't?
qa.a: Asking what could make Pia feel better turned Tanvir's attention to her feelings, and he chose a real repair.

qa.q: What did Tanvir see when his father apologised to Pia?
qa.a: He saw an adult model a real apology, which may teach him what sorry actually means.

grounding: Shows a teacher observing that a demanded 'sorry' comes out empty, while asking what would help the friend and an adult's own apology teach more.

subtype: Stage 4: Forced sorry versus felt sorry [Observer]
passage: Outside their house in the village, Swati snatched the paper windmill from her little cousin Bittu, and he howled. Her mother, Neelam, grabbed Swati's arm. "Say sorry! Right now!" Swati muttered "sorry" without looking up and kept the windmill. Dadi was watching from the charpai. Later, when Bittu cried again, Dadi called Swati over. "Look at Bittu's face. What would make him happy again?" Swati thought hard. Then she ran over, gave him the windmill, and blew on it to make it spin. Bittu stopped crying. Neelam watched quietly.

qa.q: Where was Dadi sitting?
qa.a: Dadi was watching from the charpai.

qa.q: What does Swati keeping the windmill after "sorry" show?
qa.a: It shows the sorry was forced; she said the word but didn't feel it or change anything.

qa.q: What lesson might Neelam take from watching Dadi?
qa.a: Asking Swati what would make Bittu happy led to a real repair, which worked far better than demanding an instant sorry.

qa.q: How did Bittu experience the two different sorries?
qa.a: The muttered one left Bittu still without his windmill, while the real repair made him stop crying.

grounding: Shows a mother's demand for an instant sorry producing a mumble, while a grandmother's question about making the cousin happy leads to real repair.

subtype: Stage 4: Forced sorry versus felt sorry [Observer]
passage:
At the playground in Toronto, Ivan watched Xin push his friend Leo off the swing.
Xin's dad marched over. "Xin! Say sorry. Right now."
Xin looked at the ground. "Sorry," she mumbled, not looking at Leo.
Leo was still crying.
Ivan looked at his mum. She crouched down next to Leo. "Oh, Leo, that hurt, didn't it? I'm sorry that happened." Then she asked Xin, "What could help Leo feel better?"
Xin thought, then held out her hand to help Leo up. Ivan watched Leo take it.

qa.q: Who pushed Leo off the swing?
qa.a: Xin.

qa.q: What was Ivan feeling as he watched Xin say sorry?
qa.a: He seemed puzzled and uncertain, looking to his mum because Xin's mumbled sorry didn't make Leo stop crying.

qa.q: Which approach worked better, and why?
qa.a: Ivan's mum showed a real apology and asked Xin what could help Leo, which led Xin to offer her hand, unlike the forced "say sorry" that had no feeling.

qa.q: What is Xin experiencing when her dad insists she say sorry?
qa.a: She seems embarrassed and unhappy, mumbling the word without looking at Leo.

grounding: A child watches a parent force an empty sorry, then sees another adult model an apology and ask what would make the friend feel better.

subtype: Stage 4: Forced sorry versus felt sorry [Observer]
passage:
At kindergarten pickup, Jyoti was waiting for her Papa by the gate. She saw Seema's mother pull Seema by the arm.
"You bit Rehaan! Say sorry! Now!"
Seema's face went red. "Sorry," she said to the floor, very fast. Then she hid behind her mother.
Rehaan was still holding his arm.
Jyoti's teacher came over. She knelt down and said, "Rehaan, I'm sorry you got hurt." Then she asked Seema softly, "What could we do to help Rehaan's arm feel better?"
Seema peeked out. "Ice?" she whispered. Jyoti watched her go with the teacher to get it.

qa.q: What did Seema do to Rehaan?
qa.a: She bit him.

qa.q: What was Jyoti feeling as she watched Seema's fast sorry?
qa.a: Jyoti seemed curious and a little worried, noticing that Rehaan was still holding his arm after the sorry.

qa.q: What made the teacher's approach more helpful than the forced sorry?
qa.a: The teacher modelled a real sorry and asked Seema what could help, which let Seema take part in fixing things instead of mumbling.

qa.q: What is Seema experiencing when her mother insists she say sorry?
qa.a: She feels ashamed and embarrassed, saying sorry fast to the floor and hiding.

grounding: A child at kindergarten watches a forced sorry fall flat, then sees a teacher model an apology and ask what would help the hurt friend.

subtype: Stage 4: Forced sorry versus felt sorry [Observer]
passage:
I'm Ujjwal. I'm six. I saw what happened at the birthday party.
Yamini knocked down Bunty's block tower. Bunty cried. Yamini's papa said, "Say sorry! Say it!" really loud.
Yamini said, "Sorry," but she said it like a robot and she didn't look at Bunty.
Then Bunty's mama came. She said, "Oof, that's sad. Yamini, how can we fix it?"
Yamini got down and put two blocks back. Then Bunty put two blocks.
They made it tall again.

qa.q: What did Yamini knock down?
qa.a: Bunty's block tower.

qa.q: What was Ujjwal feeling as he watched Yamini say sorry like a robot?
qa.a: Ujjwal seemed puzzled, noticing the sorry didn't seem real because Yamini didn't look at Bunty.

qa.q: Which approach helped more, and why?
qa.a: Bunty's mama asked how they could fix it, which led Yamini to rebuild the tower, showing more than the forced loud "say sorry."

qa.q: What is Yamini experiencing when her papa shouts?
qa.a: She probably feels embarrassed and upset, saying sorry like a robot without looking at Bunty.

grounding: A child describes watching a forced sorry fail and another adult asking how to fix things, which leads to a real repair.

subtype: Stage 4: Forced sorry versus felt sorry [Observer]
passage:
Monday: At the park, Ayaan grabbed Ujjwal's kite string. Ujjwal cried. His father, Imran, pulled Ayaan over. "Say sorry. Now!" Ayaan mumbled "sorry" at his shoes and ran off. Imran saw Ujjwal was still crying.

Tuesday: At home, Imran thought about the mumble. That evening he shouted at Ayaan over spilt milk, then stopped. He knelt. "I'm sorry I shouted. That wasn't kind." Ayaan stared, then hugged him.

Saturday: At the park, Ayaan grabbed the kite again. Imran crouched. "Ujjwal looks sad. What could make him feel better?" Ayaan thought. He held out the string. "You fly it first."

qa.q: What did Ayaan grab on Monday?
qa.a: Ayaan grabbed Ujjwal's kite string.

qa.q: What might Imran have been thinking on Tuesday about the mumbled sorry?
qa.a: He seemed uneasy and unsatisfied, realising the forced sorry had meant nothing to either child.

qa.q: What changed in how Imran handled Saturday, and why did it work?
qa.a: Instead of demanding a sorry, he pointed to Ujjwal's sadness and asked what would help, so Ayaan chose a real repair.

qa.q: How is Ujjwal affected on Saturday compared to Monday?
qa.a: On Monday Ujjwal kept crying after the mumbled sorry; on Saturday he gets the kite first, so he likely feels better and cared for.

grounding: A father sees a forced 'say sorry' produce a mumble, then models an apology and asks what would help, and the child repairs for real.
